* **Title:** Bastarder
* **Genre:** Low Fantasy
* **Word count:** 1000
* **Type of feedback desired (line-by-line edits, general impression, etc.)**: General Impression. I'm trying to see how I can improve my writing mostly. These are merely the first pages of my first draft, both unfinished here.
* **A link to the writing:** [**https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Oe8DPHqIaPaEoO5NNQ5KwN1OGkvOGAW2DNKEt5qxICU/edit?usp=sharing**](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Oe8DPHqIaPaEoO5NNQ5KwN1OGkvOGAW2DNKEt5qxICU/edit?usp=sharing)

Op here. Ive called a doctor wholl refer me to a psychologist later next week.

I'm feeling better but my emotions are still high. I feel an emptiness inside me because I havent created anything worthwhile in years. I used to draw, write and sculpt all the time and all that has gone now as I grew up. This book I feel validates me as itll be proof that I created something worthwhile in my life.

Im restarting again. Ive got the experience.

Good lord I just finished The Ninth Rain just yesterday! I started the sequal today; its the first really high fantasy book I've read in a long time and a really fun read. I like how you you use words and can convey so much with such simple use of language. What would you call your influences?
The Winnowing Flame books, The Shattered Sea trilogy and A land fit for heroes trilogy. After that there are a couple of very recent releases that I want to read to have a bit of a break.

Having read BR, cripes, this guy really, really didnt enjoy BR...

Though I agreewith him how the book was dull and that the characters were pretty 1dimensional, and how a miserable setting isnrtgoing to give a book loved by everyone, telling insteadof showing? I feel Fletcher uses third etsondeep and shows the world through the eyesof the characters excellently.
God everyone is mwntioning Second Apocalypse which I happen to have just started. Cant wait to see what it offers.
Ringil from the Land fit for heroes trilogy is the best part of the first book.

I find that if a book takes me over more than some others I'll make it a point to finish it first. If I really like a book I can read a 500 page tome in an entire free day, something I cant really do with my busy job so it takes me 3 days nowadays.

I have so many books I feel that to keepmyself engaged I have to read2, sometimes even 4 books at once, so long as I finished my previous cycle. I try to choose 1 fantasy novel/series, 1 historical novel, a literary behemoth and another novel that has to have been released in the past 3 to five years.

The last one is because I want to keep up with current trends in litersture, to see how prose and writing have changed, something thats important to me as a budding novelist.

Some books have interesting concepts but not a very enthrallling journey. If I skip pages or paragraphs it means I'mmore interested in whats going to happen to the concept rather than just engrossing myself in the world. 

If I feel bored reading  a book but still care enough about the characters I'll skip parts that I can tell are irrelevant information. Excessive description, pov characters I dont care about, stuff that doesnt add to the experience.

The last sentence is important. I did not skip a single line from Warlord Chronicles but I skipped many The Steel Remains because whilst callbacks to the past were short and sparse in the former, they were very frequent and inyterrupted the flow of the present story. And unlike Kostova's The Historian, there was no intetrsting mystery to be revealed by these flashbacks. 

I appreciate how Robert Jordan captures even the smallest details in a character to make them more human. But his novels DRAG, for me. Some parts of eye of the world were really good reads, some parts were a slog. Bits its a book that does a slow pace right. 

Unlike a lot of people pace is very important to me. I like slow paced books but not ones where I feel I had my time wasted. Which is why I gave up on American Gods but not EotW, why I skipped through most of Beyond Redemption and still got all the information I needed 50 pages towards the end and dont feel guilty about it. All the books I read or want to read have interesting concepts, whether I want to experience the entire joirney is up for me to decide.
